title: Where it grows
subtitle: Douro, Dão and beyond
objectives: Name countries that have adopted it

steps.title: The Douro and Dão
steps.body: Touriga Nacional is planted in most Portuguese regions, but the Douro and the Dão are its heartlands. In the hot, dry Douro, on schist, it gives powerful, concentrated wines. In the Dão, cooler and granite-based, it gives more elegant, floral wines with fresher acidity. It also grows in Alentejo, Lisboa and Bairrada.

steps.title: Climate
steps.body: Touriga Nacional handles heat and drought well thanks to deep roots and small berries. Strong sun develops its colour. In very hot sites it can lose some aromatic finesse, so higher or north-facing vineyards are valued. Its vigorous growth needs careful canopy management.

steps.prompt: Match each Portuguese region to its Touriga style.
steps.explanation: Portugal's regions bring out different sides of the grape.

steps.title: Abroad
steps.body: With warmer summers, other countries are interested. Bordeaux approved Touriga Nacional for trial in its AOCs in 2021, as a heat-tolerant option. It also grows in Spain, Australia, South Africa, where it's used for fortified wines, and California.

steps.prompt: Why did Bordeaux approve Touriga Nacional for trial in 2021?
options: It handles heat and drought well
steps.explanation: Bordeaux is looking for grapes adapted to a warming climate.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Douro and Dão are Touriga Nacional's heartlands
It handles heat and drought well
Bordeaux, Spain, Australia and South Africa grow it too
